complexity.correctness_reason: Input strings may contain any of the 256 ASCII characters, so e.g. strs = ["paysutdlfmywvaugplk49w87ky9v478"] encodes to the delimiter concatenated with itself and decodes to three empty strings instead of the original.
complexity.notes: The delimiter swap is the whole story: the previous submission's 😀 sits outside the 256-character ASCII set the statement guarantees, so it can never collide with input content, whereas this ASCII-only delimiter can. ||Prefixing each string with its length|| avoids delimiters entirely and is the standard general answer (it also satisfies the follow-up for arbitrary character sets).
complexity.summary: Joins the strings with a fixed delimiter and appends a trailing delimiter, then decodes by splitting on it and dropping the empty tail. Both passes touch each character once, so total work is linear in the character volume, which here scales as n.
